OCD patients with autogenous obsessions have a greater activation of the ventral striatum, the ventral pallidum, and the anterior insular cortex, and OCD patients with reactive obsessions have greater activation of the amygdala and the ventral palladium.

OCD with autogenous obsessions is associated with increased activation in brain regions related to cognitive control and self-referential processing, whereas OCD with reactive obsessions is associated to increased activation of regions related to salience, emotion processing and social cognition.
the neural substrates underlying OCD with autogenous and OCD with reactive obsessions are different.
